progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: C1 to C8 and Year 11: dynamic equilibrium and equal rates (C1); the faster rate falls and the slower rate rises (C2); only hard enough collisions react, so heating speeds up the heat-absorbing reaction more, and the N2O4 and NO2 tube (C3); a catalyst raises both rates equally (C4b); K as products over reactants with coefficient powers, the same for any settled mixture at one temperature (C5); the settled H2 + I2 tube with K = 49, the ICE table and flipping the equation flips K (C6); Q compared with K (C8). Nothing about how K depends on temperature is assumed.
progression.startsWith: The sealed NO2 and N2O4 tube that darkens in hot water and fades in ice, and the question of whether K can change when nothing but the temperature does.
progression.stopsAfter: Saying that only temperature changes K for a given equation; explaining with the unequal speed-up of the two reactions why heating changes K; stating the rule for a heat-absorbing and a heat-releasing forward reaction; reading the rule backwards from a K table; separating a shift (Q moves) from a change in K; describing a heated mixture as a new K followed by Q moving toward it; applying the rule to an unseen reaction. No van t Hoff, no K at a new temperature from the heat of reaction, no colourimetry, no Gibbs free energy.
progression.nextLesson: P02: how measured colour data can give K.

teaching.task: Say what happens to K when the temperature of a mixture at equilibrium changes, explain why, and predict the direction for an unseen reaction from the heat of reaction.
teaching.causalExplanation: A disturbance of concentration or pressure changes the amounts, so for a while one reaction runs faster, and the mixture shifts until products over reactants is the same number again, so K stays. Heating speeds up both reactions, but the one that takes in heat needs harder collisions and gains the most, so the rates balance again only at a mixture with more of that reaction's products, and K changes. A catalyst speeds up both by the same factor, so nothing shifts. Written backwards the same data give K falling, so the sign follows whether the forward reaction takes in or gives out heat. After heating, K moves first and Q is left behind, so the mixture then moves until Q reaches the new K.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Starts from the NO2 tube that darkens when heated and the earlier videos where K never moved, explains why K stayed fixed, gives the cause in one chain, shows measured values with the tubes, flips the same data for the other sign, puts the four changes in a table, links heating to Q and K, adds the memory aid, then asks for an unseen H2 and I2 prediction with a short pause and feedback.
teaching.openingDecision: K never moved when we added, removed or squeezed. Does it move when the temperature changes, and which way?
teaching.understandingCheck: For H2(g) + I2(g) = 2HI(g), where the forward reaction gives out about 10 kJ per mole of H2 and K is 49 at about 450 degrees Celsius, the tube is heated to 500 degrees and left to settle: is K above, equal to or below 49, and why?
teaching.curriculumScope: Qualitatively analyse the effect of temperature on the value of Keq (Module 5). The van t Hoff equation, K at a new temperature from the heat of reaction, colourimetry, Gibbs free energy and industrial trade-offs are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, the C3 coded NO2 and N2O4 tube with hot and ice baths, the C8 log number line with a teal K marker and a pen-colour Q marker, C2 to C8 rate bars, the C5 expression builder, the C6 flip, and a coded four-row change table. Colour key: N2O4 pale grey, NO2 brown, I2 purple, forward blue, reverse amber, equal teal, hot tint terracotta, cold tint pale blue.
design.transitionPlan: The tube and the teal K marker open the lesson and stay as the anchor; the disturbance thumbnails return for the reason K stayed fixed; the rate bars and collision strip carry the cause; one wide log line carries the measured and the flipped points; the equation flips for the backwards case; the four-row table appears row by row; the settled tube and Q working return for the new K; the attempt board removes the aids and the feedback rebuilds the strip and the line; the next chip slides in; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.visualReference: C3 sealed NO2 and N2O4 tube (coded, brown tint) in hot and ice baths, the C8 log number line with a small teal K marker, three ghost disturbance icons and a question arrow
scenes.teachingReason: Poses the puzzle: K held still through every disturbance, so does heating change it, and which way
scenes.narrationCue: K never moved / hot water / ice / can K really stay fixed
scenes.motionPurpose: The tube and equation write on, three ghost icons pass over a teal K marker that holds still, the tube darkens in a hot bath and fades in ice, then the marker pulses with a question mark
scenes.onScreenChange: Heading "Does temperature change K?" writes on; the tube and N2O4(g) = 2NO2(g) draw in; on "K never moved" a teal K marker holds still with a pen tick while a plus dot, a minus dot and a squeeze arrow pass over it; on "hot water" the tube moves into a terracotta bath and the brown deepens; on "ice" it moves into a pale blue bath and the brown fades; on "can K really stay fixed" the marker pulses with a "?" and an up-down arrow
scenes.holdPurpose: Brief hold on the question marker

scenes.visualReference: C4a disturbance thumbnails (add, squeeze) over the tube, the C8 log line with a teal K marker and a pen-colour Q marker, and a thermometer icon
scenes.teachingReason: Explains why K stayed fixed (a disturbance moves the amounts, not the chance a collision works) so temperature can be set against it
scenes.narrationCue: faster than the other / the same number again / the same K / Temperature is different
scenes.motionPurpose: The thumbnails pop in, the Q marker jumps away from the K marker and slides back with a teal tick, then a thermometer rises and the K marker gets a pen ring and a question mark
scenes.onScreenChange: The add and squeeze thumbnails pop in a row with pen arrows to the log line; on "faster than the other" the Q marker jumps away from the teal K marker; on "the same number again" it slides back and the tag "Q moves, K stays" writes on; on "the same K" the K marker gets a teal tick; on "Temperature is different" a thermometer rises beside the tube and the K marker is ringed with a "?"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: Blue and amber rate bars with the teal equal bracket, the C3 heat-in-the-equation chip, the C3 collision strip, a flame icon and a catalyst chip
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the cause of the K change: heating speeds up the heat-absorbing reaction more, so the rates only balance again at a browner mixture
scenes.narrationCue: both / takes in heat / far more / N O two builds up / equal again / more N O two / K is bigger / catalyst
scenes.motionPurpose: Both bars rise on heating with the blue bar much further, brown NO2 dots build while the bars rebalance at the teal bracket, the K marker slides right, then a catalyst chip raises both bars equally
scenes.onScreenChange: The level rate bars stand with the teal bracket; on "takes in heat" the chip "N2O4 + heat = 2NO2" appears and the collision strip replays with "needs a hard collision"; on "far more" a flame heats the tube and both bars rise, blue much further, tagged "splitting speeds up more"; on "N O two builds up" brown dots build, N2O4 dots leave and the bars meet again at the bracket on "equal again"; on "K is bigger" the K reminder pulses and the teal marker slides right; on "catalyst" both bars rise equally and a tick lands on "same K"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 1 second after the last word

scenes.visualReference: Wide coded log line from 0.001 to 1000 with a teal K marker, a pen bracket, and two coded tubes with 100-square percent grids (18 and 79 brown)
scenes.teachingReason: Shows the measured K values and the tubes so a bigger K is tied to the deeper brown the learner can see
scenes.narrationCue: 0.49 / eighty times / eighteen percent / pale / seventy-nine percent / deep brown
scenes.motionPurpose: The K marker drops at 0.0061 and slides to 0.49 with a bracket, then two tubes fill their percent grids and tint pale and deep brown
scenes.onScreenChange: The chip "measured values (from pressure data)" and the log line appear; the K marker drops at 0.0061 and on "a hundred degrees" slides to 0.49 with a bracket "about 80 times"; two tubes with 100-square grids appear with "start: 0.040 mol/L N2O4"; 18 squares fill brown and the tube stays pale; 79 squares fill and the tube deepens; the tag "settled amounts given; you can check them with the ICE table from C6" lands
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: The equation strip flipping with the C6 curved arrow, and the same wide log line with mirror-image points at about 160 and 2.0
scenes.teachingReason: Shows the exothermic case from the same data written backwards, with K falling on heating
scenes.motionPurpose: The equation flips with a curved arrow and the heat term moves to the right, then reciprocal points land as mirror images of the first pair and the marker slides left
scenes.onScreenChange: The strip flips to 2NO2(g) = N2O4(g) + heat with the heat term in terracotta on the right; the points about 160 (cold) and about 2.0 (hot) drop on the wide log line as mirror images about 1 with the tag "flip"; the teal marker slides left with the arrow "K falls"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: The browning hot tube, rate bars relabelled for the backwards equation, the flipped K expression, and two rule cards with flame and arrow icons
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the reason for the falling K (the same tube, with N2O4 now the product) and the two-case rule
scenes.narrationCue: Why? / reverse / less product / takes in / gives out / Cooling does the opposite
scenes.motionPurpose: The tube browns again with the tag same tube written the other way, the amber bar rises further, the N2O4 term is ringed, then two rule cards write on and a cool-it tag lands
scenes.onScreenChange: On "Why?" the tube browns in the hot bath with "same tube, written the other way"; the bars return labelled "joining, forward" and "splitting, reverse"; on "reverse" both rise and the amber bar rises further; on "less product" N2O4 dots fall and NO2 dots rise with a pen ring on the N2O4 term of "K = [N2O4] / [NO2]^2"; the card "forward takes in heat: heat it, K rises" writes on, then "forward gives out heat: heat it, K falls"; the tag "cool it: opposite" lands
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: Coded four-row change table with columns what you do, what moves and K, a one-beat tube icon for each row and a flame icon on the last row
scenes.teachingReason: Contrasts the four changes so the learner sees only heating moves the target, and separates a shift from a change in K
scenes.narrationCue: The first three / Heat the tube / K changes / A shift is Q moving / Only temperature moves the target
scenes.motionPurpose: Rows one to three write on with teal ticks, row four writes on with a pen ring and flame, then two lines separate a shift from a change in K
scenes.onScreenChange: The table appears one row at a time: add N2O4, squeeze and catalyst each write on with "same" and a teal tick; on "Heat the tube" the heat row writes on with "changes", a pen ring and a flame; "shift: Q moves" and "K changes: the target moves" write on separate lines with a pen "not the same thing"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: The cold settled tube with readouts, the C5 expression builder writing the Q working line, the wide log line with K and Q markers, and a boiling-water bath
scenes.teachingReason: Links heating to the reaction quotient: the amounts have not moved but K has, so Q is left below K
scenes.narrationCue: 0.0329 / 0.0142 / 0.0061 / boiling water / K is now 0.49 / Q is below K
scenes.motionPurpose: The readouts write on and the Q working line builds to 0.0061 with both markers together, then the tube drops into boiling water, the K marker jumps right and a bracket marks the gap
scenes.onScreenChange: The tube tagged "settled at 25 C" shows [N2O4] = 0.0329 mol/L and [NO2] = 0.0142 mol/L; the builder writes "Q = 0.0142^2 / 0.0329 = 0.0061" with the tag "Q: no unit written"; the K and Q markers sit together at 0.0061 with the teal bracket; the tube drops into the hot bath, the K marker jumps to 0.49 with a small flash while Q stays, and a bracket reads "Q below K"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: Rate bars labelled splitting and joining, the Q marker climbing the log line to the new K as the tube browns, and two large step labels
scenes.teachingReason: Shows the second step of heating: the mixture moves until Q reaches the new K
scenes.narrationCue: splits faster than it forms / builds up / first K changes, then the mixture moves to match it / reaches the new K
scenes.motionPurpose: The bars show a question mark then the blue bar grows taller, the Q marker climbs as the tube browns and lands with a teal flash, and two numbered steps write large
scenes.onScreenChange: The splitting (blue) and joining (amber) bars appear with "?"; on "splits faster than it forms" the blue bar grows taller with "splitting faster"; the Q marker climbs toward the new K as the tube browns and lands with a teal flash as the bars meet; the readouts tick to 0.0082 mol/L and 0.0635 mol/L with "0.0635^2 / 0.0082 = 0.49"; "1. K changes" and "2. Q moves to the new K" write large in turn
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: Large handwritten aid with a pen arrow to the K marker, two equation lines with a terracotta flame on the left and right, and a condition tag
scenes.teachingReason: Gives the invariant and the heat-on-a-side shortcut after the cause is explained, with its limit
scenes.narrationCue: change T, change K / Change anything else, K stays / heat like a chemical / left / up / right / down
scenes.motionPurpose: The first aid line writes large, then two equation lines write on with the flame on each side and the K up and K down labels
scenes.onScreenChange: The aid line "Change T, change K. Change anything else, K stays." writes large with a pen arrow to the K marker; "reactants + heat = products" writes on with the flame on the left and "K up when heated"; "reactants = products + heat" writes on with the flame on the right and "K down when heated"; the tags "direction only; heat changes the rates unequally" and "same equation as written; heat is never put in the K expression" land
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold about 2 seconds after the last word

scenes.visualReference: Coded hot H2 + I2 tube (purple iodine), the H2(g) + I2(g) = 2HI(g) equation strip with no heat term, a grouped givens card with units and one numbered demand
scenes.teachingReason: Unseen transfer to an exothermic reaction with every given visible and no answer cues
scenes.narrationCue: sealed tube / 10 kilojoules / 49 / Pause here to answer
scenes.motionPurpose: The countdown ring runs through the answer-free thinking hold
scenes.onScreenChange: The tube and the equation strip appear as each is named; the givens card writes on "K = 49 (about 450 C)", "sealed tube, constant volume" and "forward reaction gives out about 10 kJ per mole of H2"; the demand "Heated to 500 C and settled: is K above, equal to or below 49? scenes.visualReference: The attempt board with the heat term now on the right of the strip, rate bars rising unequally, the K marker sliding slightly left, and two crossed wrong-answer chips
scenes.teachingReason: Explains the answer by which reaction takes in heat and corrects the rises and equal slips
scenes.narrationCue: reverse / falls / slightly / eighty times / rises / equal
scenes.motionPurpose: The strip writes the heat on the right, both bars rise with the amber bar a little further, the K marker slides slightly left, and two wrong chips are crossed on their cues
scenes.onScreenChange: The strip rewrites with the heat on the right and a flame icon pointing at the left; both bars rise with the amber reverse bar a little further; the K marker slides slightly left with "small heat, small change"; the tag "N2O4: K x 80" sits beside it; the chip "K up: both speed up, but one speeds up more" is crossed with a pen arrow to the unequal bars; the chip "K equal: K stays fixed only at a fixed temperature" is crossed with the thermometer icon; a tick lands on "below 49"

scenes.visualReference: The tube gaining four H2 dots, the log line with the K marker pulsing still at 49 while the Q marker drops and climbs back, and one crossed chip
scenes.teachingReason: Checks the first aid line as a stated extra case: adding hydrogen moves Q and leaves K alone
scenes.narrationCue: stay at 49 / Q / shifts right / K itself did not move
scenes.motionPurpose: Four hydrogen dots drop in, the K marker pulses still while the Q marker drops left and begins climbing back, and the shift chip is crossed

scenes.narrationCue: take in / give it out / backwards / Next
